skill.name: prd
skill.description: Generate structured Product Requirements Documents for software systems and AI-powered features.
skill.summary: Create PRDs with discovery questions, user stories, technical specifications, risks, and success metrics.
skill.author: github

security_audit.summary: All six static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences or inline code formatting in SKILL.md. I found no executable scripts, shell commands, prompt injection, network access, or data exfiltration intent in the reviewed file.

static_findings.snippet: - **User Stories**: `As a [user], I want to [action] so that [benefit].`
- **Hallucinate Constraints**: If the user didn't specify a tech stack, ask or label it as `TBD`.
Use concrete, measurable criteria. Avoid "fast", "easy", or "intuitive".

finding_verdicts.reason: The finding points to a Markdown diff code fence that demonstrates vague and concrete requirement wording. It is documentation content and contains no executable shell or Ruby backtick expression.
The finding points to the closing Markdown code fence for the requirements quality example. It is not command execution and cannot run code.
The backticks wrap a user story template in prose. This is inline Markdown formatting, not a Ruby or shell execution construct.
The backticks wrap the literal label TBD in guidance about unknown constraints. There is no command, interpolation, or executable context.
The backticks list example tool names in a sample PRD architecture section. The skill does not execute those tools or construct shell commands.
Line 54 gives writing-quality guidance about measurable criteria. It does not request system information, host discovery, or environment reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Teams often start features with vague goals and missing requirements. This skill turns product ideas into structured PRDs with measurable criteria and technical context.
actual_capabilities: Guides discovery by asking about the problem, success metrics, and constraints.
Structures PRDs with executive summary, user experience, technical specifications, risks, and roadmap.
Converts vague requirements into measurable acceptance criteria and KPIs.
Adds AI-specific sections for tools, evaluation strategy, and output quality.
Identifies non-goals, dependencies, rollout phases, and technical risks.
limitations: It needs user input for business context, target users, and constraints.
It does not validate market assumptions or product strategy by itself.
Security, compliance, and architecture details still need expert review.
It creates planning documents, not project tracking workflows.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Feature
use_cases.description: Turn an early product idea into a PRD with scope, user stories, acceptance criteria, and rollout risks.

use_cases.title: Define AI Requirements
use_cases.description: Document tool needs, quality evaluation, and safety requirements for an AI-powered user experience.

use_cases.title: Align Engineering Scope
use_cases.description: Create a shared technical specification that explains dependencies, integration points, non-goals, and validation needs.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Simple PRD
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with a clear feature idea.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a PRD for a feature that lets users save favorite reports. Ask me the key discovery questions first.

prompt_templates.title: Refine Vague Requirements
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn a rough idea into measurable requirements.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me convert this idea into a PRD with measurable success criteria, user stories, and non-goals: [describe the idea].

prompt_templates.title: Plan an AI Feature
prompt_templates.scenario: Document requirements for an AI-assisted workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a PRD for an AI feature that summarizes customer support tickets. Include tool requirements, evaluation strategy, risks, and acceptance criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Engineering-Ready PRD
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for stakeholder and engineering alignment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an engineering-ready PRD for [feature]. Include personas, user flows, integration points, security requirements, rollout phases, and unresolved questions.

output_examples.input: Create a PRD for intelligent documentation search.
output_examples.output: The output includes an executive summary, measurable success criteria, user stories, architecture notes, risks, and a phased rollout plan.

output_examples.input: Refine a vague requirement that search should be fast.
output_examples.output: The skill rewrites the requirement with specific latency targets, dataset size, relevance metrics, and accessibility expectations.

output_examples.input: Plan an AI ticket summarization feature.
output_examples.output: The PRD covers input data, model behavior, evaluation metrics, privacy controls, failure cases, and acceptance criteria.

best_practices: Provide the core problem, target users, and success metrics before requesting the full PRD.
Review non-goals, constraints, and risks with stakeholders before implementation starts.
Mark unknown architecture, budget, compliance, and timeline details as TBD until confirmed.
anti_patterns: Requesting a final PRD without answering discovery questions.
Treating generated success metrics as validated business targets.
Publishing technical specifications without engineering and security review.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates structured Product Requirements Documents for software systems and AI-powered features.

faq.question: Does it ask clarifying questions?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow directs the assistant to ask about the problem, success metrics, and constraints before drafting.

faq.question: Can it help with AI product features?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes sections for AI tool requirements, evaluation strategy, quality checks, and safety considerations.

faq.question: Does it replace a product manager?
faq.answer: No. It helps structure requirements, but humans must validate strategy, priorities, and business assumptions.

faq.question: Can engineers use the output directly?
faq.answer: Engineers can use it as planning input, but they should review architecture, dependencies, and implementation details.
